ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a large square tile, whose interior is divided by several lines into eight congruent right triangles and a small square in the middle. Point P is on the left boundary of the large square, point Q is on the upper boundary of the large square, and segment PQ is the hypotenuse of the right triangle in the upper left corner; the two right-angle sides of this triangle are respectively along the left side and upper side of the large square. The figure also shows that each side of the large square is pieced together from one short right-angle side and one long right-angle side of this kind of congruent right triangle. Reasoning: Let the two right-angle sides of each right triangle be a and b. The area of the large square is 49 cm^2, so the side length is 7 cm, therefore a+b=7. It is known that PQ is the hypotenuse and has length 5 cm, so a^2+b^2=25. From (a+b)^2=a^2+b^2+2ab, we get 49=25+2ab, so 2ab=24, ab=12. The area of each right triangle is ab/2=6 cm^2, and the total area of the eight triangles is 8×6=48 cm^2. The area of the small square equals the area of the large square minus the area of the eight triangles, namely 49-48=1 cm^2.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify that PQ is the hypotenuse of a corner right triangle, whose two legs lie along two adjacent sides of the large square. Let the congruent triangle legs be a and b. The same visual tiling shows each side of the large square is made from one leg of length a and one leg of length b, so a+b=7 because the tile area is 49 and hence its side length is 7. From the text, the hypotenuse is 5, so a^2+b^2=25. Use (a+b)^2=a^2+b^2+2ab to get 49=25+2ab, hence ab=12. Each right triangle has area ab/2=6, so the eight triangles have area 48. Subtract from the whole tile area: 49-48=1 cm^2 for the small square.
